nodes.dezerter_po.text.t: Hieronim strokes his beard. "Tomasz? He's holding up. Good that someone talks to him. A man who runs from the Empire rarely has anyone to open his mouth to." He falls quiet, then adds, more softly: "If someone's always going to be hunting him, he'd better have people around him."

nodes.dezerter_po_wydany.text.t: Hieronim says nothing for a long while. "You gave him up. You had your reasons, and I won't pretend you didn't. But Tomasz sat by my stove, ate my soup and told me about the cats he loved as a boy. Things like that stay in a man like a splinter. Don't come to me about it again."

nodes.dlug_po.text.t: Hieronim sits down heavily, his hands shaking so badly he has to press them to his knees. "A voice. Of course, a voice. Thirty years I counted the stars and not one of them said a word to me. And you, who've barely dragged yourself up here… Well. It isn't fair, but that's the world for you. Whatever you decided, I hope it was you who decided it, and not that thing for you."

nodes.glusz_po.text.t: "They'll manage. Not because they're strong, but because they've no choice. But remember: everyone who stayed behind now watches the imperial patrols and thinks of you. That's no reproach. It's just how things are."

nodes.lodz_plotka.text.t: "The first? Two days after the spark storm. Two days west of our hills there's a hull of iron and glass lying on the ground. Don't go there at night, because at night something walks about."

nodes.obserwatorium.text.t: Hieronim sighs as if he'd been saving that sigh up for thirty years. "The Emperor ordered the stars counted. The stars fell, so he ordered us to count where. They fell where they had no business falling, so he ordered us to keep counting. Now nobody counts any more, because whoever counted knows too much. That leaves me, Brygida and Comet. Comet's the cat. A nasty one."

nodes.p1.options.[p1a].text.t: A wanderer who ran from the Imperials.

nodes.p1.options.[p1b].text.t: Someone who saw the stars fall.

nodes.p1.options.[p1c].text.t: The Commander at Wolf's Ford knows who I am.

nodes.p1.text.t: Hieronim lowers the tool he was holding like a flail. "A roof I've got. Quiet it isn't. First things first: who are you, good sir? And don't say nobody, that's the meanest answer I know. Nobody comes up here for nothing. Everyone's got something on his conscience or in his pocket."

nodes.p2.options.[p2a].text.t: From Głuszec, but it ended badly.

nodes.p2.options.[p2b].text.t: Through the forest, any way I could.

nodes.p2.text.t: Hieronim takes off his spectacles and wipes them on a sleeve dirtier than the lenses. "Ran, saw, knows. Like everyone. And where have you come from? Because the road through Głuszec has been shut for a fortnight."

nodes.p3.text.t: "Badly, well, all the same. Nobody here asks about your past, only about what you can do. Do you know how to handle a broken machine? A fickle sky? A cat that hates everyone?" Hieronim eyes you with suspicion. "Don't answer. I'll take you in. Comet may have other ideas, mind."

nodes.p_koniec.text.t: Hieronim nods with the satisfaction of a man who's just won a bet against himself. "Brygida didn't run you off? That's rare. Good. Here's ten groats and an offer: if you ever want to get into something deeper than a roof, come and see me. There are a few things lying on the far side of the hills that need measuring."

nodes.powitanie.options.[dlug_po].text.t: Brygida fitted the core. I heard a voice.

nodes.powitanie.options.[lodz_plotka].te.t: Where did the first star fall?

nodes.powitanie.options.[obserwatorium]..t: Why does this place stand empty?

nodes.powitanie.options.[p_koniec].text.t: I've met Brygida. Got a roof. No quiet, but a cat and frayed nerves.

nodes.powitanie.options.[q10_jeszcze].te.t: I think it's time for the crater.

nodes.powitanie.options.[q10_ostatnie].t.t: I did what you asked. What's your question?

nodes.powitanie.options.[q10_start].text.t: I think it's time for the crater.

nodes.powitanie.options.[q2_start].text.t: Need anything from the Glass Field?

nodes.powitanie.options.[q3_odrzucil].te.t: I turned down the stones' bargain.

nodes.powitanie.options.[q5_koniec].text.t: I found him and led him out.

nodes.powitanie.options.[q5_start].text.t: Has anyone gone missing around here?

nodes.powitanie.options.[q8_a].text.t: Any news coming in from Głuszec?

nodes.powitanie.options.[q8_b].text.t: Any news coming in from Głuszec?

nodes.powitanie.options.[q9_nie].text.t: The soldier said no, but I'm not done with him.

nodes.powitanie.options.[q9_po].text.t: The soldier at the Watchtower agreed.

nodes.powitanie.options.[q9_start].text.t: Who else keeps watch over these parts?

nodes.powitanie.options.[szkla].text.t: What are those shining fields all around?

nodes.powitanie.text.t: Hieronim stands by the broken telescope with the face of a man who's just been told his life's work is nothing but a guess. "A stranger? A stranger indeed. Everyone who drags himself up here is a stranger. Come to measure something, or just to warm yourself, eh?"

nodes.q10_jeszcze.text.t: Hieronim shakes his head. "Not yet. You've got loose ends, and nobody comes back from the crater to tidy up trifles. It's the point of no return. Finish what you started, or drop it with a clear conscience, and then come."

nodes.q10_nie.text.t: Hieronim sits back down and looks out of the window, where there's nothing to see. "Aye, well. Someone has to stay put for when people come back. Or don't." He's silent for a moment. "Go, before I change my mind."

nodes.q10_pytanie.options.[nie].text.t: Stay here. Someone has to mind the telescope.

nodes.q10_pytanie.text.t: Hieronim looks at you without his spectacles, and only now do you see he has the eyes of an old man who's stared at the sky too long. "The question's simple. Do you want me to come with you? I'm old, foolish, and my hand shakes. But I know maps and I know where to look. If not, then not. If so, I vouch for nothing."

nodes.q10_start.text.t: Hieronim takes off his spectacles and lays them on the table as if saying goodbye to them. "Yes. I know. When someone comes in wearing a face like that, the parting of the ways is near. Before you go, talk to Brygida. She has something for you that I can't give. Then come back to me, because I have one question." This is the point of no return: after this talk you set out for the crater. And from there the road runs east, three days to the Camp on Crow Mountain, where the imperial army stands facing the Jarnowians and press-gangs anyone who can't hide fast enough.

nodes.q10_tak.text.t: Hieronim gets up, and suddenly there's a spring in him nobody would have suspected. "Good. I'll take the maps, I'll take the cat, I'll even take a flask of vodka. They may not come in handy, but better to have than to go looking." His smile is honest and a little scared.

nodes.q2_koniec.text.t: Hieronim picks the shards up with tongs and lays them side by side on a tray. The light in them flickers, each to its own rhythm. "They remember. The green still knows the earth, the blue still the sky, and the red… that one burns. Good work. Take twenty groats from the Starwatch coffers. The last we've got, so don't drink them away at the first tavern."

nodes.q2_start.text.t: "Shards. Three of them, each a different colour. The green remembers the earth, the blue the sky, the red fire. I'm measuring how fast they lose their memory. Bring them to me, only don't carry them against your skin, and don't stare into any of them too long. If you go cold inside your skull, throw it away. No, don't throw it away, for God's sake. Bring it."

nodes.q3_odrzucil.text.t: Hieronim looks at you longer than is proper. "You refused. Nobody before you ever refused. I wouldn't have dared. Either you're a fool or you've got something I lack. Here's fifteen groats for telling me the truth."

nodes.q3_przyjal.text.t: Hieronim goes pale and sits down. "You took it. So now it owes you something. Or rather, you owe it. I don't know if that's good or bad, but I know nothing comes free. I hope you knew what you were agreeing to. Here's fifteen groats for the research."

nodes.q3_start.text.t: "The standing stones. Twelve of them, each with one face like a mirror. They talk. Not in words, but in what they remember. Go near and they'll offer you something like a bargain. I never know whether to take it or not. Go, listen, then come and tell me. Only remember: every bargain has its price. Every last one."

nodes.q5_koniec.text.t: Hieronim drags a hand down his face as if checking it's still there. "Alive. Not talking, but alive. Tell Brygida to give him some soup. Did he say anything about deserting? Because whoever comes out of that fog rarely comes out the same as he went in."

nodes.q5_start.text.t: Hieronim flinches as if someone had named his sins to his face. "There's a fog lying in the Hollow that eats sound. Three days ago one of the Imperials went in there, the one Brygida patched up and who stayed on with us. He wanted to see how far the silence reaches. He never came back. If he's still alive, he can't call for help. Find him before the fog chews him up."

nodes.q8_a.options.[nie].text.t: Don't send anything. Let them fend for themselves.

nodes.q8_a.text.t: "A man came by yesterday with a bundle on his back. Said there'd been a manhunt. The Imperials lit fires in the square, questioned everyone left standing and rode off at dawn. Grumble the innkeeper lived, but the tavern lost its shutters. Wawrzyn the reeve keeps wailing that he was never anybody, only the reeve. They asked about you. I can send them a bit of coin, but it's your money, not mine."

nodes.q8_b.text.t: "A man came by with a letter from Grumble. He writes that the Imperials poked around the village but took nobody, because nobody knew anything. Wawrzyn sends his regards and told me to say he knows nothing, and hopes you don't either. The village is whole, but folk have stopped trusting each other, and every man eyes his neighbour as if he were ill luck itself. I can send them a bit of coin to drink the fear away. It's your money, not mine."

nodes.q8_nie.text.t: Hieronim nods, with no judgement in his face. "So be it. Nobody saves everyone. Only remember that in Głuszec they'll remember this too." He goes back to the telescope, but his hand is shaking.

nodes.q8_wyslij.text.t: Hieronim counts the coins, wraps them in a rag and hands them to the boy waiting by the door. "To Głuszec. Quick as you can. And don't tell anyone who sent it." He turns to you. "Foolish of you. But decent." Three wanderers who'd been hanging about by the gate look at you with respect.

nodes.q9_nie.text.t: "He said no. No wonder, the man's made of granite. Don't let it gnaw at you. Some people you can't win over, you can only outlast."

nodes.q9_po.text.t: Hieronim claps his hands, which with him looks like he's swatting a mosquito. "A soldier! A real one! The Empire will think we're raising an army. Let it think so, and then we'll all be surprised, indeed we will." He hands you fifteen groats.

nodes.q9_start.text.t: "On the northern ridge stands the Last Watchtower. An old soldier sits up there who served the Emperor and now serves nobody. His men have scattered, but they know where to find him. If you ever need muscle, look for it there. Only he's stubborn as a rock and just as talkative."

nodes.szkla.text.t: "Glass? It's not glass, good sir. It's something that passes itself off as glass so folk won't pick it up. It was left over from the fall. Every piece remembers how it was flung down. If you ever touch one and go cold inside your skull, don't say I didn't warn you."

nodes.w_toku.text.t: Hieronim looks up from his maps. "You've got a few things half done, and you know it. You didn't drag yourself up here to loll about on the stove, but to finish what you started. You've got your journal, so look in it. And if you can't remember where you were meant to go, you need either a longer sleep or a shorter memory."
